fact: The Education Sector Plan 2023-2027, the ministry's costed plan, says the 'traditional EMIS' of routine administrative tasks and student head counts will be expanded into a real-time, integrated EMIS ecosystem with data down to class and student level, decentralised digital data entry, a digital profile of each student and a link to the national ID, and gives 'strengthen EMIS' a programme and an expenditure line in each subsector including primary; no date is given for the statement, so the document's published date is used.

The Education Sector Plan 2023-2027 lists EMIS as a department of the Ministry of Education and Technical Education and makes the ministry responsible for building the planned integrated EMIS ecosystem; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.
The ministry said the platform will start in several education departments in 2026/2027 before gradual national expansion; no school count is given.
The platform is to give teachers digital tools to record attendance and absences and to monitor each student's performance and assessment results, with the ministry receiving updated data daily.

The education ministry signed an agreement with the Japanese company SPRIX on 10 August 2026 (announced that day) for a nationwide attendance, performance and assessment platform, starting in 2026/2027.
The Ministry of Education and Technical Education signed the agreement and says the platform is part of its integrated national digital system for managing and monitoring education.
